prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

An interface for positive pressure respiratory therapy includes a mask assembly having a mask seal and a mask shell. The mask assembly is positioned lower than and exposes a bridge of the user's nose. The mask seal includes first and second portions on respective first and second sides of a nasal region that contact opposing sides of the user's nose. In some configurations, the first and second portions each include supports that help maintain a shape of the mask seal. A pair of covers can be supported relative to the mask assembly and adjacent a respective one of the first and second portions of the mask seal. The covers limit expansion of the first and second portions of the mask seal in response to pressurized air within the mask seal. The supports of the first and second portions can transfer load from the mask seal to the covers. An interface system can include multiple size mask seals, which can be designed with consideration of ethnic variations in nose size and/or shape.

An interface for positive pressure respiratory therapy may include a mask assembly configured to deliver pressurized breathing gas to a user. The mask assembly can include a mask seal and a mask shell, which together define a structure suitable for positioning on the user’s face and forming a sealed breathing interface.

In use, the mask assembly is positioned below the bridge of the user’s nose, leaving the bridge of the nose exposed rather than covered. This arrangement can improve comfort and reduce pressure on sensitive areas of the face, particularly around the nasal bridge. The mask seal may include first and second portions that contact opposing sides of the user’s nose. These portions help form a seal around the nasal region while accommodating the contours of the user’s face.

The mask assembly may also include one or more supports, covers, or similar reinforcing components. These features can help maintain the intended shape of the mask seal during use. In particular, they can limit unwanted expansion or deformation of the mask seal that may occur when pressurized air is delivered through the interface. By helping the seal retain its shape, these components can improve sealing performance, stability, and user comfort.

The interface system may further include a range of mask seal sizes. The different sizes can be designed to accommodate variations in nose size, nose shape, and facial anatomy among different users. In some implementations, the sizing options may account for ethnic variations in nasal geometry, helping provide a better fit for a broader user population. This can improve the effectiveness of positive pressure respiratory therapy by supporting a more reliable seal and a more comfortable user experience.
outputs.L4:
A positive pressure respiratory therapy interface includes a mask assembly configured to sit relatively low on a user’s face, leaving the nasal bridge substantially exposed. Instead of extending over the bridge of the nose, the mask forms a seal along the lower and side regions of the nose. This arrangement can improve comfort for many users by reducing contact with sensitive areas near the nasal bridge and by helping to keep the user’s field of vision less obstructed.

The mask assembly includes seal portions positioned along both sides of the user’s nose. These seal portions are supported by corresponding structural supports that help maintain the intended sealing shape during use. Adjacent cover portions are also provided near the seal portions. The covers cooperate with the supports to control how the seal behaves when the mask is exposed to positive airway pressure, such as during CPAP, bi-level, or other respiratory therapy.

During operation, pressurized gas delivered to the mask can cause flexible sealing components to expand or deform. The supports and adjacent covers limit excessive outward expansion of the side seal portions, helping the seal remain properly positioned against the face. By controlling this movement, the mask can reduce leakage and improve stability without requiring excessive headgear tension. The supported construction also helps distribute forces from the mask and headgear more effectively, allowing loads to be transferred through the mask structure rather than being concentrated only at the soft sealing regions.

This load transfer can contribute to a more secure and consistent fit, particularly when the user moves during sleep or when therapy pressure changes. Because the nasal bridge is not used as a primary sealing surface, the interface may also reduce the likelihood of discomfort, soreness, or pressure marks in that area. The low-profile arrangement may be especially useful for users who are sensitive to traditional masks that contact the bridge of the nose.

The interface may be produced in multiple sizes or configurations to accommodate a wide range of facial anatomies. In particular, the shapes and dimensions of the seal portions, supports, and covers may be varied to suit differences in nose width, height, projection, and sidewall contour. These variations can help address ethnic and individual differences in nose shape and size, providing improved fit options for a broader patient population.

Overall, the respiratory therapy interface combines a low-positioned mask design with supported side sealing structures and adjacent expansion-limiting covers. This configuration helps maintain seal integrity under positive pressure, improves load distribution, and promotes a stable and comfortable fit across different users and mask sizes.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the most common and important words in the English language. Although it is very short, it plays a big role in making sentences clear and specific. The word “the” is called a definite article, which means it points to a particular person, place, thing, or idea.

For example, when someone says, “I saw the dog,” they are talking about a specific dog that the listener may already know about. This is different from saying, “I saw a dog,” which could mean any dog. In this way, “the” helps give meaning and direction to communication.

The word “the” appears in everyday speech, writing, books, news, songs, and conversations. It may seem simple, but without it, English would sound less natural and less precise. Small words like “the” remind us that even the simplest parts of language can be very powerful.

counterfactuals.output: A patient interface for delivering positive pressure respiratory therapy includes a mask body configured to seal against a user’s face below the nasal bridge while supplying pressurized breathable gas to the user’s nares. One or more support structures are associated with the side seal portions to assist in maintaining seal geometry and stability during use. In some configurations, a cover or restraint element extends over or adjacent to at least part of the mask body to limit outward expansion or deformation of the side seal portions when the mask is pressurized. The patient interface may be provided in a plurality of sizes and/or shapes having different nasal widths, heights, contours, or side seal configurations to accommodate different nose geometries while maintaining a seal below the nasal bridge.

counterfactuals.output:
The invention is a CPAP mask assembly designed to fit a wider range of users by accounting for differences in nasal anatomy, including ethnic variations.

It includes:

- A mask shell and flexible seal that form a breathing chamber around the user’s nose.
- First and second side portions of the seal positioned along the sides of the nose.
- Structural support members associated with those side portions to help maintain seal shape and stability during use.
- Cover portions adjacent to the nasal side portions, likely improving comfort, sealing performance, or appearance.
- A sizing/configuration approach in which the geometry of the nasal seal is selected or shaped based on variations in nose size and shape among different populations.

In short, the patent claims a CPAP nasal mask whose seal and supporting structure are specially shaped and sized to improve fit, comfort, and leak resistance across users with different nasal anatomical characteristics.
